title: Bounded-limit preserving space-valued presheaves are filtered colimits of representables
statement:
Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets and $\kappa$-filtered infinity categories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and the spaces, coherent functors, transformations and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means in the fixed smaller universe $\mathcal U$; $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $A$ be a small infinity category admitting $\kappa$-small colimits, and put $\mathcal P(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Write $y:A\to\mathcal P(A)$ for $y(a)=\operatorname{Map}_A(-,a)$. For every $X\in\mathcal P(A)$ the following are equivalent:

(1) There exist a small $\kappa$-filtered infinity category $I$ and a coherent functor $p:I\to A$ such that $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{I}(y\circ p)$ in $\mathcal P(A)$.

(2) For every $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$, every coherent diagram $q:K\to A$ and every colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_Ka$ in $A$, the map of spaces
$$X(a)\longrightarrow\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k)),$$
obtained by applying the contravariant functor $X$ to the components $\lambda_k:q(k)\to a$ together with their coherences, is an equivalence. The empty simplicial set $K=\varnothing$ is included: then $a$ is an initial object of $A$, the limit is a terminal space, and (2) requires $X(a)$ to be contractible.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, printed p. 404 (PDF page 422): equivalence of (1) and (3) when A admits kappa-small colimits. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this space-valued quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal P(A)$, which has small mapping spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], and let $B\subset P$ be the full subcategory of objects equivalent to representables. The Yoneda functor is fully faithful by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] choose a coherent quasi-inverse $k:B\to A$, with counit $yk\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$. The target-fixed slice right fibration $P_{/X}\to P$ is classified by $\operatorname{Map}_P(-,X)$, by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Pull it back along $y$ and write $E=A\times_P P_{/X}\to A$. Its classifier is $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_P(y(a),X)\simeq X(a)$, naturally by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation]. The classification theorem permits a small right-fibration model $p:I\to A$ for this classifier since $A$ and all $X(a)$ are small. The equivalence of classifiers gives inverse maps with coherent inverse homotopies over $A$ between $I$ and $E$. In particular, their total quasicategories are equivalent. An object is a pair $(a,x)$ with $x\in X(a)$, and the corresponding arrow $y(a)\to X$ is given by Yoneda evaluation.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.1.5.2 and Corollary 5.3.5.4 proof; smallness via straightening/unstraightening.

proof.text: Let $C=B\times_P P_{/X}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density], its source projection has a canonical colimiting cocone to $X$. Since $y$ takes values in $B$, $E=A\times_B C$ degreewise, and $r:E\to C$, $(a,u)\mapsto(y(a),u)$, is the projection of this pullback; it keeps the arrow $u$ to $X$. The projection $P_{/X}\to P$ is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] with $K=\Delta^0$, so its pullback $\pi:C\to B$ is a right fibration, horn lifting problems pulling back; in particular $C$ is a quasicategory and $\pi$ is an inner fibration. Passing to opposites exchanges $\Lambda^n_i$ with $\Lambda^n_{n-i}$ and preserves equivalence edges, so $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a left fibration of quasicategories. The last clause of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift], applied to $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the universe $\mathcal U'$ in which all these quasicategories are small, gives for each $c\in C$ and each equivalence edge $\pi(c)\to b'$ of $B$ an equivalence edge of $C$ with source $c$ lying exactly over it. Thus $\pi$ is an isofibration in the sense used by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit]. That statement, with $T=A$ and $g=y$, gives for every quasicategory $Q$ an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A)^\simeq\times^h_{\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)^\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}(Q,C)^\simeq$ compatible with the projections. Postcomposition with $k$ is an inverse of $y_*$ up to the natural equivalences $ky\simeq\mathrm{id}_A$ and $yk\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$ of step 1 whiskered by $Q$; these whiskered transformations are equivalences in $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)$ because their vertex components are equivalences ([lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]), hence paths in the cores. Hence $y_*:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,A)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,B)^\simeq$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. The projection of a path-space pullback along a homotopy equivalence is a homotopy equivalence, so $r_*:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)^\simeq\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,C)^\simeq$ is one for every $Q$. Taking $Q=C$, a point over $\mathrm{id}_C$ gives $s:C\to E$ with an equivalence $rs\simeq\mathrm{id}_C$; taking $Q=E$, the points $sr$ and $\mathrm{id}_E$ have equivalent images $rsr\simeq r$, so $sr\simeq\mathrm{id}_E$ because $r_*$ is injective on components. Thus $r$ is a functor equivalence over the projections to $P$, and it carries the arrows to $X$ identically. Reindex this cocone by the equivalence $I\simeq E\simeq C$. It remains colimiting: restriction along an equivalence and its quasi-inverse gives inverse equivalences on the spaces of coherent cocones with any fixed apex, so preserves the universal mapping-space property of the cocone. Its underlying diagram is $yp$ and its components are the arrows corresponding to fibre points. Thus $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I yp$, with $I$ small. No filteredness is asserted yet.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.1.5.3; explicit reindexing of its canonical representable-slice cocone. Comparison E≃C written via the isofibration pullback statement (Kerodon/HTT invariance of right fibrations under base equivalence).

proof.text:
Assume (1), with small $\kappa$-filtered index $J$ and $t:J\to A$. For a $\kappa$-small $q:K\to A$ and colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$, objectwise presheaf colimits (small colimits exist in $\mathcal S=\mathcal P(\Delta^0)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]) and the contravariant representable colimit-to-limit property in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$X(a)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_A(a,t(j))\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j)).$$
Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to the coherent diagram $(k,j)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j))$, the restriction of the coherent mapping bifunctor $H_A$ of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] along $q^{\mathrm{op}}\times t$, to obtain
$$X(a)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k)).$$
Taking opposites does not change the number of nondegenerate simplices, so $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is still $\kappa$-small. Every comparison is induced by the legs of $\lambda$: after evaluation at $j,k$ it is precomposition by $q(k)\to a$. The naturality clauses of both cited statements retain these maps and coherences. Hence the displayed equivalence is exactly the specified comparison in (2). Both cited statements allow $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: HTT Corollary 5.3.5.4, (1) implies (3), using Proposition 5.1.2.2 and Proposition 5.3.3.3.

proof.text:
We record the section calculation used next, directly from the cited mapping-space formulas. For a small simplicial set $K$ and $q:K\to A$, put $F=Xq^{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $\Gamma_q$ be the space of sections of $q^*I\to K$. The dual classification in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies
$$\Gamma_q\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta *,F).$$
More generally, it identifies maps $T\to\Gamma_q$ with transformations $\Delta T\to F$, because the constant functor $T$ classifies $K\times T\to K$ and a map $K\times T\to q^*I$ over $K$ is exactly a $T$-parameter family of sections. By the limiting-cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], these transformations are $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,\lim F)$, naturally in $T$; the limit exists by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Thus $\Gamma_q\simeq\lim F$, with restriction to each vertex and its coherences the actual section evaluations. For a cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$, a point $x\in X(a)$ induces the section with values $X(\lambda_k)(x)$. This is the pullback/constant-functor mapping-space formula of the classification statement applied to $\lambda$, so it includes all higher simplices. To spell out the compatibility assertion, regard $\lambda$ as the map $K\times\Delta^1\to A$ from $q$ to the constant diagram at $a$. Its pullback right fibration has classifier $X\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$, that is, the arrow $\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(a)\to F$ with components $X(\lambda_k)$. By the classification mapping-space formula, a section over this cylinder is a coherent transformation from the terminal functor to that arrow diagram. Fixing its endpoint sections to be $r$ and the constant point $x$, such a transformation is a coherent square whose remaining datum is a path from the composite $\Delta *\xrightarrow{x}\Delta X(a)\to F$ to the point of $\operatorname{Map}(\Delta *,F)$ represented by $r$. A path in the reverse direction gives this path by inversion, since this mapping object is a space. The same description for parameter spaces $T$ retains the higher compatibilities. Under classification this section is a map $K\times\Delta^1\to I$ over $\lambda$ with those endpoints, hence exactly a transformation $r\to\Delta_K(a,x)$, which is a cocone by definition.

source.place: HTT Corollaries 3.3.3.3-3.3.3.4 (dual section model for limits); calculation written from the cited classification formula and the limit definition.

proof.text: Assume (2). For a $\kappa$-small diagram $r:K\to I$, let $q=pr$. By step 4, its section data correspond to a point $s\in\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k))$. By the hypothesis on $A$ choose a colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$. Condition (2) makes the actual restriction map $X(a)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k))$ an equivalence. An inverse equivalence supplies a point $x\in X(a)$ and a path from its image to $s$, with all higher compatibility data. The last clause of step 4 makes these data a coherent cocone from $r$ to $(a,x)$ in $I$. For $K=\varnothing$, $a$ is initial, the limit is terminal, and (2) makes $X(a)$ contractible and in particular nonempty; this again gives a cocone. Thus every $\kappa$-small diagram in $I$ admits a cocone, precisely the definition of $\kappa$-filteredness in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

source.place: HTT Corollary 5.3.5.4, expanded proof of (3) implies (2), using the section calculation in step 4.

proof.text: The small index $I$ of step 2 is now $\kappa$-filtered by step 5. Its projection $p:I\to A$ and the colimiting fibre-point cocone from step 2 therefore give exactly the presentation required in (1). This proves (2) implies (1); step 3 proves the reverse implication.
